authorizationFindings: IMAGING_CLINICAL_ROLES = [OWNER, ORG_ADMIN, CLINIC_MANAGER, DENTIST, RECEPTIONIST]; IMAGING_MANAGE_ROLES = [OWNER, ORG_ADMIN, CLINIC_MANAGER] (imaging.ts:68-69). Legal-hold mutation is restricted beyond the general clinical-role set on both attachment models: PATCH .../attachments/:id/legal-hold and PATCH /imaging/studies/:id/legal-hold both require OWNER or ORG_ADMIN only (attachments.ts:288, imaging.ts:927).

authenticate middleware (middleware/auth.ts:104-196) computes allowedClinicIds from UserClinic rows, rejects if no accessible clinic, cross-checks resolved clinic.organizationId === user.organizationId, and rejects on suspended/cancelled clinic status.

Backup/restore is authenticated (not role-differentiated authorized): every route under server/src/routes/platformAdmin.ts:152 (including the 7 backup/file-backup routes at lines 1553-1660) is gated only by authenticatePlatformAdmin, a single-tier check (server/src/middleware/platformAuth.ts, interface at lines 9-16 has only {id, email, sessionId} — no role/tier field exists on the platform-admin principal at all).

No step-up re-authentication (TOTP/password) is applied specifically to the backup/restore-triggering routes — verifyTotp is used only at platform-admin login/TOTP-setup/TOTP-verify endpoints (platformAdmin.ts:100,202,227), not in the backup section (1550-1660).
auditFindings: auditImaging() helper (imaging.ts:103-121, wraps writeAuditLog) covers device/request/study/bridge CRUD, view events (imaging_study_viewed on every preview/download), legal-hold changes, and bridge lifecycle events; metadata payloads are documented and test-verified to exclude filenames/patient identifiers/UIDs (imaging.test.ts:263-271).

attachments.ts writes AuditLog entries for legal-hold set/release and delete-blocked-by-hold, explicitly excluding the free-text legalHoldReason from audit metadata (attachments.ts:341-344 comment: 'no PII in audit log').

A SEPARATE table, ActivityLog (via utils/activity.ts logActivity()), DOES include original filenames in its description string for PatientAttachment upload (attachments.ts:161-170) and delete (attachments.ts:444-453) — this is a distinct code path from AuditLog and was not found to apply the same filename-redaction discipline.

writeAuditLog() (utils/auditLog.ts:37-58) is fire-and-forget and swallows all errors (console.error only) — an audit write failure does not fail the underlying request and is not otherwise surfaced. writeAuditLogInTx() (78-97) is transaction-scoped and non-swallowing but is used elsewhere (clinicBulkExportPackage.ts), not by imaging/attachment routes.
imagingBridgePublic.ts logs imaging_bridge_heartbeat_first_seen, imaging_bridge_study_ingested (metadata excludes filename/patient data), and imaging_bridge_pairing_redeemed.
storageFindings: server/src/services/fileStorage.ts is the single storage abstraction for both PatientAttachment/LabOrderAttachment and ImagingImage bytes; local-disk (uploads/<clinicId>/...) by default, S3-compatible when S3_BUCKET is set (fileStorage.ts:1-22).
buildStorageKey(clinicId, originalName) (fileStorage.ts:71-74) bakes clinicId into the storage key as the first path segment — tenant isolation is structural, not just a query filter.

isSafeStorageKey() (fileStorage.ts:144-155) rejects absolute POSIX/Win32 paths, UNC prefixes, and '..'/'.' traversal segments; a prior host-OS-dependent bug (Windows-style absolute paths passing on Linux) is documented as fixed in a comment referencing PR #160.
No signed-URL generation exists anywhere in fileStorage.ts (confirmed by full-file read) — see signedUrlFindings.

No at-rest encryption logic exists in fileStorage.ts itself; S3 server-side encryption, if any, would be bucket-level infrastructure configuration, not application-enforced — not confirmed in this pass (evidence gap).

No checksum/integrity verification exists on the PRIMARY upload path (attachments.ts / imaging.ts manual-upload route) — checksums are computed only for bridge-upload dedup (server-recomputed sha256 against client-claimed ingestKey, imagingBridgePublic.ts:247-252) and for FileBackupEntry copies (sourceChecksumSha256/destinationChecksumSha256).

deleteFile() (fileStorage.ts:467-474) performs a hard physical delete (S3 DeleteObjectCommand or fs.unlink), idempotent on ENOENT. For PatientAttachment it is called only after a confirmed single-row Prisma delete (attachments.ts:439). For ImagingImage there is NO delete endpoint at all — deleteFile is invoked only as compensating cleanup when a DB transaction fails after a file was already saved (imaging.ts:683-684; imagingBridgePublic.ts ~385), never as a user-facing lifecycle operation.

Forward orphan detection exists (orphanFileInspection.ts: DB row present, physical file missing -> storageVerifiedMissingAt, informational only, never triggers deletion). Reverse orphan detection (physical file present, no DB row) is explicitly NOT implemented (orphanFileInspection.ts comment, lines 16-22).

server/src/services/fileBackupService.ts explicitly never mutates primary storage (header comment, lines 1-31): 'NEVER modifies, renames, or deletes anything in primary storage... NEVER changes a PatientAttachment/LabOrderAttachment/ImagingImage/ImagingStudy row.' Confirmed: deleting a source PatientAttachment row does NOT delete its FileBackupEntry or destination object (dbVerification/fileBackupDbIntegration.test.ts:331, described in-test as 'disclosed gap, confirmed live').

signedUrlFindings.currentState: No signed-URL mechanism exists anywhere in the inspected scope. All Imaging and PatientAttachment binary access (preview/download) streams bytes through the authenticated Express process via openFileStream() -> res, gated by authenticate + authorize(roles) + validateAndGetClinicIdScope on every single request. imaging.ts explicitly documents this as an intentional design principle (Turkish comment, lines 8-19: images never get a public URL).
signedUrlFindings.responseHardening: streamStudyImage() sets Cache-Control: private, no-store and X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff on every image response (imaging.ts:782-783) and writes an imaging_study_viewed audit event on every access.
signedUrlFindings.futureRequirement: If Imaging is ever extracted to a separate deployable/service (out of scope for this task to authorize), the current per-request re-authentication model would need to be replaced or fronted by a short-lived signed-URL / token-exchange contract, since a separate service cannot reuse the monolith's in-process session/role checks directly. This is a contract requirement for a FUTURE state, not a current gap — current behavior is a deliberate, tested design choice.

anonymizationFindings: redactPatientImagingImages(clinicId, patientId) (patientAnonymization.ts:103-131) performs METADATA-ONLY redaction: sets ImagingImage.originalName to '[ANONYMIZED]'. The underlying image bytes (DICOM/CBCT pixel data, JPEG/PNG content) are never touched, deleted, or scrubbed by this function.
The same function skips redaction entirely when the parent ImagingStudy has legalHold = true, incrementing counters.skippedLegalHold (lines 112-115).
redactPatientAttachments() applies the identical metadata-only pattern to PatientAttachment.originalName (lines 66-95).
Called from anonymizePatientData() on both the idempotent re-run path (lines 200-201) and the first-run path (lines 347-351).
physicalDeletionFindings: PatientAttachment: exactly one delete path exists in the codebase (attachments.ts DELETE route, verified by an explicit in-code comment stating no other route/service calls prisma.patientAttachment.delete() or deleteFile() on a PatientAttachment row). Deletion is a single atomic prisma.patientAttachment.deleteMany({ where: { id, patientId, ...scope, legalHold: false } }) closing a TOCTOU window against concurrent legal-hold placement; physical file removal happens only after a confirmed delete count of 1.

ImagingImage/ImagingStudy: no user-facing delete endpoint exists at all. Physical deleteFile() calls occur only as compensating cleanup on failed upload transactions. This matches the documented KVKK posture in deletionReviewInventory.ts that imaging/clinical data is 'conservative-retain by design... pending legal sign-off', and that a prior live-delete endpoint (POST /patients/:id/privacy/deletion-review/execute) was removed entirely rather than hardened.
backupFindings: FileBackupEntry/FileBackupRun are ledger-only tables (schema.prisma:3179-3182: immutable once written, a durable per-run audit trail, not current state) — confirmed by fileBackupService.ts header comment.

fileBackupService.ts and fileBackupDestination.ts contain zero authorize/role/RBAC keyword matches (grep-confirmed) — no access-control logic exists inside the backup service itself; all authorization is external, applied at the calling route.

iterateSourceRows() (fileBackupService.ts:102-116) scans PatientAttachment/LabOrderAttachment/ImagingImage across ALL clinics with no clinicId filter; tenant isolation for backups is enforced only at the destination-key layer (buildBackupDestinationKey(domain, clinicId, sourceRecordId) -> file-backups/{domain}/{clinicId}/{sourceRecordId}.bin).

The calling route for backupService.ts (previously 'not located' per PZ-IMG-03 in F2-PREP-002) is now identified: server/src/routes/platformAdmin.ts, via dynamic import at lines 1555/1568/1579/1598 (backupService.js) and 1619/1630/1650 (fileBackupService.js).

All backup/file-backup routes (platformAdmin.ts:1553-1660) sit behind router.use(authenticatePlatformAdmin, csrfProtection('platform')) applied once at line 152. authenticatePlatformAdmin validates a JWT of type platform/platform_admin and sets req.platformAdmin = {id, email, sessionId} — no role or tier field exists on this principal.
No step-up authentication (TOTP/password re-verification) is applied to the backup/restore routes specifically; verifyTotp is used only at login/TOTP-setup/TOTP-verify endpoints.

platformBackup.test.ts asserts only binary auth ('missing token -> 401', 'valid platform token -> sets platformAdmin', 'clinic-type token rejected with 403') — no test asserts a specific platform-admin role/tier is required for backup or restore.

Confirmed via dbVerification/fileBackupDbIntegration.test.ts:331: deleting the source PatientAttachment row does NOT delete its FileBackupEntry row or destination object — described in-test as a disclosed, confirmed-live gap. This means backup copies of imaging-adjacent files can outlive an erasure/anonymization action on the source.
kvkkFindings: Anonymization of imaging data is metadata-only (originalName field), not content-level — actual DICOM/CBCT/image bytes are never redacted or destroyed by the current anonymization pipeline. Whether this satisfies KVKK anonymization requirements for diagnostic imagery is a legal question this task does not and cannot resolve.

Backup copies do not inherit source-row deletion or anonymization — a confirmed, tested gap (see backupFindings). This is directly relevant to KVKK erasure/rectification propagation and must be characterized by legal/compliance before any closure claim.

Imaging binaries/metadata do not appear to be included in the KVKK patient data export package (exportFindings) — potentially relevant to a data-subject access request scope; requires legal confirmation of whether imaging is in-scope for that export.

Legal-hold is a first-class, audited safeguard (OWNER/ORG_ADMIN-only mutation, blocks both anonymization and deletion) on both PatientAttachment and ImagingStudy — a positive control already in place.

AuditLog metadata is deliberately PII-minimized for imaging events (IDs/modality/counters only, tested); ActivityLog is not held to the same discipline and carries original filenames for attachment operations — filenames are user-supplied and could incidentally contain patient-identifying strings; this has not been assessed and is recorded as a gap, not a violation.
This section defines required safeguards to preserve and gaps to close; it does not assert KVKK legal closure for Imaging, which remains outside this task's authority.

pzImg03Status.detail: Direct evidence now shows the backup/restore routes (server/src/routes/platformAdmin.ts:1553-1660) are gated by authenticatePlatformAdmin (single-tier session authentication) plus CSRF protection. This is authentication, not role-differentiated authorization: the platform-admin principal (middleware/platformAuth.ts:9-16) carries no role/tier field, so no evidence distinguishes a restricted-support role from a full-restore-capable role, and no step-up re-authentication gates these specific endpoints. Per task governance, PZ-IMG-03 is preserved as unresolved/OPEN because direct evidence of backup RBAC (role-differentiated authorization) was not found — only single-tier authentication was found.

step-up re-authentication specifically applied to POST /backups/run, /backups/restore-test, /file-backups/run, or /file-backups/restore-rehearsal

risks.summary: Backup copies of Imaging/attachment files are not deleted or redacted when the source row is deleted or anonymized (tested, confirmed).
Imaging anonymization is metadata-only; DICOM/CBCT pixel data and image bytes are never scrubbed.
fileBackupService source-row scan is not clinicId-filtered (cross-tenant read at scan time within a platform-level service); isolation relies solely on destination-key structure.
PZ-IMG-03: backup/restore routes have single-tier platform-admin authentication, no role-differentiated RBAC, no step-up auth on the restore-capable endpoints specifically.
writeAuditLog() is fire-and-forget and silently swallows failures — AuditLog completeness is not guaranteed for imaging/attachment events.
ImagingImage.clinicId consistency with its parent ImagingStudy.clinicId is an application-level assumption, not a DB-enforced constraint.
ActivityLog descriptions carry original (user-supplied) filenames for PatientAttachment operations, unlike the PII-minimized AuditLog — filename PII exposure has not been assessed.
At-rest encryption for primary imaging/attachment storage (S3 SSE or equivalent) was not confirmed as enabled/enforced in this pass.
Imaging data does not appear to be included in the KVKK patient privacy export package (grep-level finding, not fully confirmed).

contractRequirements: An explicit LegalHold contract spanning PatientAttachment.legalHold and ImagingStudy.legalHold (already flagged as a candidate in F2-PREP-001) rather than the current direct cross-table field access.
A backup-erasure-propagation contract: when a source row is deleted/anonymized, define whether and how FileBackupEntry-tracked backup copies must be redacted or purged, and by whom.
A backup RBAC contract: role-differentiated platform-admin permissions plus step-up authentication for restore-capable operations, required before PZ-IMG-03 can be considered for closure.
A signed-URL / access-token exchange contract for the future state where Imaging is served by a separate deployable, replacing today's in-process authenticate+authorize+scope check per request.

A query contract for Imaging's outward references to Patient/Appointment/TreatmentCase (currently direct FK reads), consistent with the general future-query-contract direction noted in F2-PREP-001/002.
A reverse-orphan-cleanup contract (physical file present, no DB row) — currently unimplemented by design (documented gap in orphanFileInspection.ts).
An export-completeness contract clarifying whether Imaging data must be included in the KVKK patient privacy export package.
A DB-level (or transactionally-enforced) invariant that ImagingImage.clinicId always equals its parent ImagingStudy.clinicId, replacing the current application-level assumption.
limitations: This is a code-evidence assessment only. It does not constitute a legal KVKK compliance determination, does not authorize module extraction or caller migration, does not modify Prisma schema/migrations/tests/routes/services, and does not implement dependency-cruiser.
